name: hauling-gate
description: Self-dispatching debris hauling (issue #552, superseding the manual 'vehicle haul <id> fragment:<id>' flow from #437): once a debris_hauler and a truck-licensed driver exist, an on-ground blast fragment spawns its own haul_debris PendingAction with no player command at all — the driver claims it, boards the free hauler, drives to the fragment, loads it only on arrival, drives to the nearest freight_warehouse, and delivers it only on arrival. There is no player-chosen fragment id any more (findReachableGroundFragment's nearest-reachable pick happened at claim time instead), so this file only advances ticks and asserts on the automatic outcome: logistics.storedMassKg must rise, and by the final tick block the hauled fragment must read state:stored.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 4 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(25,25) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

expect.note: the driver already holds driving.truck at level 1 from ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION -- this call is a same-level no-op

steps.description: #552: auto-dispatch spawns the haul_debris PendingAction the moment a fragment lands on_ground with a licensed driver and a free hauler available -- there is no manual click gating it any more, so storedMassKg is no longer pinned to 0 here (the driver may already be under way, or even have delivered, well inside this window). Only cash's upkeep drain is still asserted.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul <id> fragment:<id>' step -- there is no player-chosen fragment id any more (findReachableGroundFragment's nearest-reachable pick happens automatically at claim time, the same selection the old Haul button used to make on click), and no button to wait for or click. Just letting the clock run is the whole action; automatic dispatch does the rest.

expect.note: storedMassKg is deliberately not asserted to an exact value here: automatic dispatch's own fragment choice (findReachableGroundFragment, run at claim time instead of on a player click) is sensitive to the driver's exact tick-by-tick position, and interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (Finding #12) can in principle pick a different -- but equally valid -- fragment than command mode's clean tick10. Left as increased/under-asserted-exact rather than hard-pinning a specific kg figure, since the prior tick 20 step's increased:[storedMassKg] already proves delivery completed at all -- not re-asserting the amount a second time.
